Updated assessment with Beige Book + SLOOS overlay:

- Policy signal: Modestly dovish. The FOMC cut the target range by 25 bp to 4.50–4.75% with balanced-risk guidance and continued balance sheet runoff. Implementation moves (IORB to 4.65%, ON RRP to 4.55%, ongoing caps for Treasury/MBS runoff) support easier front-end conditions while keeping some term-premium pressure via QT.
- Labor and inflation: The statement notes further easing in labor-market tightness and continued (but incomplete) disinflation—consistent with the Beige Book’s reports of softer hiring needs, improved worker availability, and moderating wage growth, alongside slower but still positive price increases.
- Beige Book overlay: District reports point to modest overall growth, mixed consumer spending (with a cautious holiday outlook in some areas), soft-to-mixed manufacturing, and persistent CRE headwinds—especially in office. Credit availability remains tight and loan demand subdued, aligning with a cautious business tone despite slightly better supply-side conditions (easing labor and slower prices).
- SLOOS (late 2024) corroboration: Banks tightened standards for small-firm C&I and subprime consumer credit; CRE standards tightened broadly. Demand was weaker for small and middle‑market firms, with some offsets (multifamily standards eased at large banks; foreign-bank C&I demand firmer; RRE/HELOC standards broadly unchanged).
- Implications: The rate cut and balanced guidance are supportive, but Beige Book and SLOOS both indicate restrictive bank credit and uneven demand that will likely mute the growth impulse. Inflation progress reduces the odds of renewed tightening, yet ongoing QT and CRE/credit frictions argue for restraint.
- Net: Maintain a mildly positive stance but trim the score to reflect Beige Book-confirmed tight credit and uneven activity.
